source_status: Witkowski et al., Incentive-Compatible Forecasting Competitions, Management Science, published online 2022 final issue 2023, DOI 10.1287/mnsc.2022.4410. Already known mechanism prior art. No novelty claim.
A: Under a hypothetical SINGLE-BINARY-EVENT TWO-FORECASTER competition, does awarding deterministic winner purely by quadratic score incentivize a more extreme report than the agent's subjective true belief, despite Brier score itself being strictly proper; does a bounded quadratic-score lottery instead reward truthfulness?

B.H_det: Deterministic score-winner can be strategically manipulated in published single-event winner-take-all context.
B.H_lottery: Quadratic two-player lottery win probability 1/2+(S_i-S_j)/2 is bounded and strictly proper in expected win chance.
B.null: For the frozen numerical case deterministic truthful and misreport win chances equal, or lottery misreport increases win chance.
B.strong_rival: PFL currently might have no winner-take-all tangible prize or utility based on rank; this formal counterexample cannot establish actual users game the leaderboard. An ELF-like mechanism for one independent event does not automatically solve multiple correlated geopolitical questions.

C.scope: Exact arithmetic, no stochastic simulation or human study: two forecasters; forecaster belief p=11/20, rival fixed q=3/5; truthful r=p, deliberate more extreme r=61/100. One binary outcome x in {0,1}.
C.deterministic: winner has larger S; tied forecasters get 1/2 chance each
C.proof_identity: E_{X~Bern(p)}[lottery(p,q,X)-lottery(r,q,X)]=(r-p)^2/2 >=0. Algebraic identity proven in report; grid tests are checks, not proof continuum.
falsifiers: deterministic expected win deviation not greater than truthful
ELF expected win deviation greater than truthful
lottery non-normalized or negative at any report tested
code implies PFL prizes implemented or real causal effect
C.multiplicity: One pre-frozen counterexample plus identity, eight adversarial/structural test groups; no effect search.

D.runtime: Native Python stdlib Fraction, isolated offline

G: Independent strong mechanism prior Witkowski et al. The mathematical result is existing literature and not human experimental replication; no human original data accessed.
